title: Global Height Pairings from Admitted Green Classes
subtitle: Assembly, reciprocity, adjunction, and model comparison
summary: The proved normalized height on the intersection of all local obstruction kernels, the Strong Green implication for full Chow groups, correspondence adjunction, and comparison on supplied admissible models.
status: Internal proofs; full-domain existence remains conditional
evidence: Propositions 2.1–2.7 provide the stated analytic and geometric foundations. H16 uses the all-completion kernel; PH16 Theorem 7.5 still assumes Strong G in both complementary degrees. HA16 and MM16 retain their exact common-domain and supplied-model scope.

The Chow-invariant actual obstruction and curved pairs for every prescribed cycle are established in [1, Theorem 1.1]. The companion paper [26] organizes the geometric cases for local obstruction vanishing. Proposition 2.4 (Immersion germs). For an algebraic closed immersion i:M↪Pi:M\hookrightarrow Pi:M↪P of reduced pure-dimensional varieties, restriction identifies the degreewise actual germs along MMM with the actual sheaf of MMM. On a smooth quasiprojective ambient open, an actual form on the closed subspace admits a degreewise extension. If its restriction is DDD-closed, the derivative of the extension has zero germ along the closed subspace. The same germ statement applies to a scalar form equal to a specified constant near a closed point or zero on an ordinary neighborhood in the source. Ordinary smooth locally finite partitions produce the cutoffs used in Section 5.

Proof. The source is [13, Lemma , Theorem and Corollary ]. On an affinoid closed immersion, lift the finitely many units of an actual moment presentation through the affinoid quotient; they remain units on an ordinary ambient neighborhood of the chosen point. This proves surjectivity on germs.

For injectivity, embed the ambient variety locally into a smooth affine space and lift the form there. Choose a smooth algebraic locally closed stratum of MMM containing the scheme point under the analytic point. In characteristic zero such a stratum exists, including when MMM is singular. A smooth closed immersion has an ordinary local analytic retraction. In a unit presentation, each unit and the pullback of its restriction have the same norm on a sufficiently small ordinary neighborhood, because their difference vanishes along the stratum. The actual forms therefore have the same germ. Zero restriction implies zero ambient germ, which proves injectivity. Locally finite smooth partitions assemble the unit lifts into a degreewise extension on the stated smooth ambient open. Since restriction commutes with DDD, the derivative of any extension of a DDD-closed form has zero germ along MMM. The scalar assertions are the degree-zero cases. This proves the singular-source interface used in Section 7 without assuming a retraction onto the whole singular carrier. ◻

Pullback on actual Bott–Chern cohomology is injective for dominant maps of smooth projective varieties, and for finite constant extension with the original absolute value. Proof. The Chow map, model independence and genuine morphism-pullback compatibility follow from [1, Theorem 1.1]. Before restriction to the homological kernel it is a graded ring map: apply rational Adams projectors to model virtual bundles and use the strict tensor-product character identity; this is [11, Proposition ]. Proposition 2.3 gives finite-extension injectivity by the normalized trace.

For dominant detection, the all-actual projective-bundle diagonal homotopy gives the Bott–Chern and Aeppli bundle formulas. The mixed relative-form sequence for a smooth-center blowup identifies the pullback kernel with its exceptional Aeppli quotient. The bundle formula and localized normal-Chern extensions make that quotient zero. These are [20, Theorems and ]. The finite trace, divided by its native degree, first descends a supplied primitive to that modified target; blowup injectivity descends its class to the original target. Factor an arbitrary smooth-projective morphism as a graph immersion followed by a projective-space projection. For the latter, the algebraic Chow projective-bundle formula and actual integration give the same top coefficient of the curvature class. This proves proper kernel stability. Proposition 2.6 (Model forms and good reduction). Model Chern forms satisfy the strict identities of their operational Chern classes, and their top actual products agree with the native model measures on the normal models used below. The numerical detector kills the actual curvature of a pure operational model class that has zero intersection degree against every vertical testing cycle on each special component. On a regular model, the leading Chern character of a cycle resolution represents that operational class; the cap/Adams identification is compatible with this detector.

On a smooth projective good-reduction model, a geometrically homologically trivial cycle has zero actual obstruction. For a fixed cycle closure, the supported-complex choice has zero curvature and vanishes on the tube outside that closure. Consequently a disjoint pair with disjoint closures has zero local pairing for this choice. For a model complex with purely vertical support, the generic-acyclic Green construction is global actual.

Proof. The model-form assertions are [25, Theorems and ]. For a pure operational model curvature, wedge with arbitrary global model Hessians. The native top measure has masses equal to vertical intersection degrees on a common model refinement. Operational projection reduces each mass to a vertical testing cycle on the original model, so the assumed numerical vanishing kills every mass. Stokes and uniform density of scalar model functions then replace the Hessian factors successively by smooth ones, testing a fixed signed measure at each step. A nonzero pure actual coefficient is detected locally by a positive smooth Hessian, giving a contradiction. Local flag sections extend this detector to model vector bundles and prove their strict operational identities. The recursive model-measure comparison keeps the native special-fiber multiplicities.

On a regular projective model, the rational Chern-character-and-cap map is an isomorphism by [8, Lemma 42.58.1, Tag 0FEX]. Its unique preimage of a pure codimension-rrr class is a 2r2^r2r-eigenvector for the Adams operation ψ2\psi^2ψ2; consequently all other operational character degrees vanish. This identifies the degree-rrr term of a cycle resolution with the operational representative used by the detector. No equality after capping is silently substituted for an arbitrary operational identity.

For a smooth good model, resolve the flat closures of the specified cycle components on that fixed regular projective model. Smooth proper base change takes geometric homological triviality to the special fiber, where it annihilates every numerical testing cycle. The detector makes the model curvature literally zero. Above the model open disjoint from the full support, each line map of Proposition 2.2 is a model isomorphism and has norm one; its scalar Green factor, and hence its trace, is zero on that tube. This proves the vanishing for disjoint closures. Purely vertical complexes have empty generic support, so Proposition 2.2 gives their global actual Green forms. These arguments impose no assertion that numerically admissible lifts exist on every bad-reduction model. ◻

Proposition 2.7 (Geometric domains used in the domain corollary). The local obstruction vanishes in each of the following sectors over the fixed KKK:

  1. the complete geometric homological one-cycle group in codimension n−1n-1n−1 on a smooth projective nnn-fold with n≥2n\geq2n≥2, and all geometric homological degrees when n≤3n\leq3n≤3;

  2. all geometric homological degrees on a supplied projective-bundle tower over a smooth projective geometrically integral base of dimension at most three, and on the target of an everywhere-defined projective dominant morphism from such a tower after finite constant extension;

  3. all geometric homological degrees on a geometrically uniruled fourfold, or on a geometrically unirational variety of dimension at most five;

  4. the degrees supplied by rational domination: all degrees for a source of dimension at most five whose complete geometric homological kernel has zero original-field obstruction, and the individual ranges r≤2r\leq2r≤2 or r≥m−2r\geq m-2r≥m−2 for a source and target of the same dimension mmm with zero source obstruction in degree rrr;

  5. geometrically algebraically trivial classes in every degree;

  6. all geometric homological degrees on abelian varieties and on varieties admitting, after finite constant extension, a rational Chow diagonal identity through Tate twists of abelian varieties. This includes finite products of smooth projective geometrically integral curves.

All morphisms, model witnesses and Chow identities are required in their stated fields and degrees. A one-cycle conclusion supplies only that factor of a height pairing unless the complementary factor is separately supplied. The local abelian assertion and the motivic transfer include descent to the original field and its full actual test space.

Proof. The one-cycle argument uses a generically finite semistable alteration of the same dimension. The regular-model curve theorem constructs the numerical witness upstairs, and Proposition 2.5 descends its zero obstruction. Its complete proof is [23, Theorem ]; the weighted divisor-kernel and native multiplicity-trace proof of its model input is [12]. The divisor and degree-zero zero-cycle endpoints then give all degrees in dimensions at most three. The algebraic projective-bundle and geometric cohomology decompositions put each coefficient of a homologically trivial tower class in the homological kernel of the base. The curvature ring and pullback identities therefore give zero obstruction on the tower. Dominant detection gives the stated morphism images, retaining the original-field interpretation after finite extension.

For a rational map resolve its source by smooth-center blowups. The Chow blowup summands of a source of dimension at most five have centers of dimension at most three. In the two outer ranges the required center summands are divisors, one-cycles or zero-cycles. Proper kernel stability from Proposition 2.5 transfers those summands into the blown-up source, after which dominant detection applies. This gives exactly [22, Theorems , and Corollary ]. A geometrically uniruled fourfold admits, after finite extension, a dominant rational map from S×P1S\times\mathbf P^1S×P1 with SSS a smooth projective threefold. The tower argument supplies the source kernel, and the dimension-at-most-five rational-domination result applies. No claim for an arbitrary higher-dimensional rational source is used. The companion paper [26] organizes these geometric deductions and their complementary-degree restrictions.

Geometric algebraic equivalence is annihilated by the compact-parameter argument of [11, Theorem ]. For abelian varieties, Künnemann’s local theorem over a complete DVR with finite residue field supplies, after finite extension, the exact special-fiber complex and homology injection that correct a cycle extension to zero component cycle classes; see [6, Sections 5.5–5.8 and Theorem 6.6]. The numerical detector and native finite descent give the original-field obstruction vanishing; the deduction is [24, Theorem ]. Apply the Chow-kernel covariance of Proposition 2.5 to each factor of the supplied rational Chow diagonal and then finite-extension injectivity. This proves the motivic assertion. 10. The remaining construction problems

For a general XXX, the local problem is to construct actual strong Green forms for every specified geometrically homologically trivial cycle over each original completion FvF_vFv​. One sufficient route is the vanishing of oXFvr\mathfrak o_{X_{F_v}}^roXFv​​r​; another is a direct exact-support construction, to which Theorem 7.5 applies. The distinction is retained throughout the principal-push proof.

The model route asks for numerically admissible lifts on a supplied regular model. Theorem 8.6 and Corollary 9.3 explain exactly how such lifts compute the height. Their existence in the general middle degree is an additional geometric problem. The framed scalar calculation in Theorem 8.3 identifies the information that a comparison proof must retain: the differential and vertical support of the perfect complex, not only its absolute KKK-class or curvature.

After construction, positivity, nondegeneracy and arithmetic finiteness form a separate programme. They require information on the height radical and on the integral structure of the residual cycle groups. In families, continuity of the biextension metric and boundary estimates require uniform control that is stronger than the finite-place support statement for one fixed pair. These problems do not enter the proofs of rational-equivalence descent or correspondence adjunction above.

abstractHtml: We construct a normalized real Beilinson–Bloch height from ordinary actual non-Archimedean Green forms. The proof uses the actual-form calculus, finite trace, projective-bundle integration, and supported-complex constructions established here and in the cited companion proofs. A finite-flat base-change calculation and a supported Chern-character identity give point and proper-intersection residues for the concrete Green pair. These identities imply the principal transformation law, independence of Green choices, reciprocity, finite support in the sum over places, and rational-equivalence descent on the local obstruction-zero domains. A second principal-push construction gives the full height from a strong Green hypothesis itself, without a converse obstruction criterion. We also prove Chow-correspondence adjunction and compare the pairing with supplied regular numerically admissible models. The latter comparison yields scalar descent through an admissible alteration and an explicit formula for a supplied abelian Chow factorization.
